 Revenue at 7 Trillion Won, Operating Profit at 505.3 Billion Won
Customer Reward Program, One-Off Property Gains Weigh on Results
Cumulative AX Orders Climb More Than 20%
 Business | Published 2026.11.10. 10:09:57 | By Kim Ki-hyuk coldmetal@sedaily.com | Summary | Save A A A A view of KT's Gwanghwamun Building West wing. Photo courtesy of KT KT (030200.KS) posted weaker third-quarter results, weighed down by a base effect from one-off property sale gains a year earlier and the cost of a customer reward program. Even so, corporate orders for its artificial intelligence transformation business kept growing at a double-digit pace and key group affiliates expanded, laying the groundwork for a rebound, the company said.
 KT said on the 10th that consolidated third-quarter operating profit fell 6.1% from a year earlier to 505.3 billion won ($345 million). Revenue slipped 1.8% to 6.9975 trillion won ($4.78 billion).
 Operating profit declined mainly because of a base effect from one-off real estate sale gains booked in the same period last year. A customer reward program that ended in July and higher spending on the AI transformation, or AX, business also weighed on earnings. Profit contributions from major group affiliates in data centers, real estate and content, however, increased.
 Wireless service revenue fell 3.9% from a year earlier as subscribers left during the fee-waiver period. Still, it has been recovering since July on the launch of flagship smartphones and stronger sales of premium plans.
 Fixed-line revenue fell 1.8% from a year earlier on weaker demand for landline phones and lower advertising and pay-per-view revenue in the media business. Broadband and IPTV subscribers rose 1.4% and 0.5%, respectively.
 Cumulative orders in the business-to-business and AX segments for the first three quarters, by contrast, rose more than 20% from a year earlier. The company said related revenue would begin to materialize in earnest from the fourth quarter, backed by large contracts including AI data centers, or AIDC, and network construction for AI computing centers.
 KT also detailed infrastructure investment to expand the AX business. Aiming to build AI data center capacity of more than 1 gigawatt by 2031, the company plans to bring six new data centers online in stages, starting with Bucheon in 2027 and followed by Gaebong, Gunsan, Yongin and Ansan.
 KT completed a 250 billion won ($171 million) share buyback in September and decided on a cash dividend of 600 won per share for the third quarter. The dividend will be paid on the 12th. "The third quarter was a period in which we gave concrete shape to our AX growth strategy and sustained growth at core group affiliates, even amid changes in the business environment at home and abroad," said Min Hye-byung, KT's chief financial officer. "Going forward, we will restore profitability in our core telecom business and accelerate B2B and AX growth to do our utmost to enhance corporate value as an AX platform company."
